title: Resumable handoff tokens and escape-handshake for streaming structured JSON
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Streaming structured JSON responses (tool calls / function outputs) often end up truncated mid-token or contain escaped characters that make resumptions ambiguous. Existing resume approaches assume clients can parse fragments or simply re-request from the last byte; that leads to duplicated objects, inconsistent tool-call boundaries, and failure modes across older SDKs. Goal: Define and implement a compact 'handoff/escape-handshake' protocol that makes fragments resumable and idempotent, and provide an SDK compatibility shim so older clients can interoperate without changing wire format.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime emits fragment metadata for every JSON fragment when streaming structured outputs: fragment_seq, fragment_type (partial|final), resume_token (opaque), and optional checksum (crc32).
Client SDKs can detect truncation using fragment_type and resume_token and resume from a safe boundary without duplicating tool-call invocations.
Escaped payloads (backslash, unicode escapes, embedded newline) are encoded with an explicit escape-level header so resumption does not require full JSON reparsing from stream start.

Compatibility shim: older SDKs that do not send 'Accept-Resume: 1' continue to work; the server falls back to a best-effort lossy-repair mode and emits an advisory field 'compat_warning' in final fragments.
End-to-end tests and chaos tests (mid-stream drop at various offsets) show <1% repair failures and no duplicated tool-call executions in 1000 randomized runs.
design_decision: Use an opaque resume_token (HMAC over model+request+fragment_seq) to avoid leaking model internals and make tokens revocable.

Escape-handshake: include an 'escape_level' integer in the control envelope. When non-zero, decoder knows to apply byte-level unescaping on resume rather than attempting JSON concat. This simplifies handling of multi-byte unicode escapes and partial escape sequences.

Server will never re-run external tool hooks (webhooks/DB writes) for fragments marked 'partial' - only when a final fragment for a logical tool-call is confirmed. This prevents duplication for retried/resumed streams.

Compatibility: for legacy clients, provide server-side best-effort reassembly and an opt-in header 'Accept-Resume: 0/1'. If unspecified, server assumes Accept-Resume:1 for modern clients but keeps backward behavior for older ones and logs a compat_warning in the final envelope.
implementation_notes: Runtime: add FragmentEmitter which attaches envelope metadata to every chunk. Minimal CPU overhead: compute checksum using streaming CRC32, generate resume_token using HMAC-SHA256 with per-request nonce.
Resume protocol: client sends POST /v1/resume with resume_token and last_ack_seq to request next fragment range. Server validates HMAC and returns remaining fragments starting at next seq.
Idempotency: include logical_tool_call_id in envelope when fragment contains tool-call boundaries. Server only executes side effects when final fragment with final:true is acknowledged by client.

SDK shim: add 'streaming.resume.v1' to JS/Python SDKs. Also implement server fallback: if SDK omits Accept-Resume header, include compat_warning string in final envelope rather than failing the stream.

Framing: use ASCII-delimited envelope markers so existing stream readers that expect lines can still function. Avoid binary framing to maximize compatibility with server-sent events and simple HTTP/1.1 chunk readers.
testing_plan: Unit tests for FragmentEmitter: validate envelope format for partial/final fragments and checksum correctness.
Integration tests: simulate random mid-stream TCP drops at byte offsets (start/middle/end of multibyte escape) to ensure resume returns identical logical JSON after reassembly.
Chaos tests: enable fault-injection on production-like staging (k8s node reboots, connection resets) and assert no duplicated tool-call side effects using test webhooks that record invocation counts.
Compatibility tests: run older SDK builds (pre-resume header) and validate server emits compat_warning and reassembly still produces final JSON for 95% cases.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): deploy FragmentEmitter behind feature flag to canary runtime pool and exercise with synthetic workloads (1-2 days).
Phase 2 (beta): enable for 20% of hosted API traffic with streaming.resume.v1 advertised to SDKs and opt-in toggle; collect telemetry for resume success/failure and compat_warning rates (1 week).
Phase 3 (default): flip feature flag to 100% after QA and leak-rate <0.5% across all regions; coordinate with SDK release and docs. Provide a 2-week overlap where server accepts both compat modes.
